learningJourney.title: What is a Materialized View Refresh Strategy

explanation.foundation: Unlike a standard SQL `VIEW` (which re-executes the query on every read), a **materialized view (MV)** persists the precomputed result set on disk and indexes it.
explanation.core: Its **refresh strategy** determines how base-table mutations propagate to the MV: **full recomputation** (`REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW`), **non-blocking concurrent diff-merge** (`CONCURRENTLY`), or **Incremental View Maintenance (IVM)** / CDC stream deltas.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Materialized View Refresh Strategies, watch how what is a materialized view refresh strategy interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Materialized view refresh precomputes and updates expensive joins or aggregations on disk so analytical queries read in milliseconds, trading bounded staleness and write/refresh overhead for read speed.

learningJourney.title: Why AccessExclusiveLock and Refresh Overlap cause outages

explanation.foundation: Joining 500M-row fact tables on every dashboard load saturates disk I/O and blows past 200 ms API budgets.
explanation.core:
Yet naive MV refreshes cause two severe production incidents:
- **AccessExclusiveLock Read Outage**: running `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` *without* `CONCURRENTLY` in PostgreSQL blocks all `SELECT` queries for minutes, piling up API threads.
explanation.deepDive: - **Refresh Overlap Spiral**: as data grows, a 5-minute cron job takes 7 minutes; overlapping runs contend on locks and peg DB CPU at 100%.

ideas.title: Advisory Lock Overlap Guard
ideas.description: Wrap scheduled refreshes in `pg_try_advisory_lock(key)` so overlapping runs skip cleanly instead of piling up, and alert when duration > 70% of interval.

ideas.title: Unique Index Prerequisite
ideas.description: PostgreSQL `CONCURRENTLY` requires at least one `UNIQUE` index on the MV to compute the row-level diff.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Materialized View Refresh Strategies without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, choose full concurrent refresh for simple batch dashboards, and incremental or CDC-driven refresh when tables exceed tens of millions of rows or require sub-minute freshness.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Materialized View Refresh Strategies experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

costs: Unindexed MV scans are just as slow as base tables.

knowledgeCheck.question: What happens in PostgreSQL if you run REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW without CONCURRENTLY on a production dashboard view?

options.text: It updates only the rows that changed since the last refresh
options.feedback: Standard REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW always recomputes the entire view.

options.text: It acquires an AccessExclusiveLock, blocking all concurrent SELECT queries until the full refresh completes
options.feedback: Correct: always create a UNIQUE index and pass CONCURRENTLY in production to keep reads non-blocking.

options.text: It automatically drops all indexes on the view
options.feedback: Indexes remain, but readers are blocked for the duration of the refresh.
